text: At high SNR, the Shannon-Hartley theorem implies that doubling the bandwidth versus doubling the signal power have very different effects. Which statement is correct?
choices: Doubling bandwidth adds ~1 bit/s/Hz; doubling power doubles capacity
Doubling bandwidth roughly doubles capacity; doubling power adds only ~1 bit/s/Hz of spectral efficiency
explanation: Capacity is linear in bandwidth but only logarithmic in power, so doubling B nearly doubles C while doubling power adds just ~1 bit/s/Hz at high SNR. This is why bandwidth is more valuable than power in that regime; the reversed and equal-effect options contradict the logarithmic dependence.
